I hate the statement that seems to be flooding science media right now, "The Voyager One space probe has entered interstellar space."

It is grossly inaccurate. Sensors on the probe began detecting a pressure differential and increased electromagnetic activity due to particles interacting with deep space. Scientists working on the project believed that this phenomenon indicated that the probe was reaching the the boundary of our system. They also stated that it would take a decade or more to pass through it.

Since then, about 2012 (this didn't happen in the 90s), they have found objects that orbit the Sun that have extended this range greatly. Meaning that this is the boundary of most physical matter in the Solar System and not the edge of our system.

The Voyager probe hasn't left the Solar System, and won't for some time.
